newsitem.title: USA: Hundreds in Mass. ask about Prudential settlement.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds in Mass. ask about Prudential settlement.

text.p: Hundreds of consumers have contacted Massachusetts officials with questions about a multi-million settlement with Prudential Life Insurance after the state attorney general began runnning a series of ads.
More than 500 consumers called within six hours after the ads began airing on television and radio on Monday, the attorney general's office said Tuesday.
The television ads show Mass. Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, who has said he will run for governor in 1998, sitting behind a desk and talking about the settlement.

"Because of Prudential's practices, an estimated 30,000 Massachusetts consumers and hundreds of thousands of consumers nationwide now hold life insurance policies they thought would be paid in full long ago," Harshbarger said in a press release.
Many of the calls to Harshbarger's office were from consumers who needed help filling out claim forms or from those who had not heard about the settlement, said spokeswoman Debbie Banda.

In February, Prudential reached a nationwide agreement to settle claims that its agents engaged in more than a decade of deceptive sales practices. Prudential will pay a minimum of $410 million in restitution to policyholders and the total could reach $1 billion, the attorney general's office said.
Prudential began sending out claim forms to more than 240,000 consumers in Massachusetts alone several weeks ago.
